summary.headline: United Spirits Q2 FY27 EBITDA fell 4.3% to Rs 600 crore, with P&A price-mix up 7.4% and marketing spend at 11.6% of net sales.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 EBITDA declined 4.3% to about Rs 600 crore, with a net profit margin of about 14% and net profit of Rs 462 crore, down 2.1%. Management cited West Asia cost inflation of about Rs 50 crore in the quarter, weaker lower-end consumer demand, and a Maharashtra and Karnataka policy drag on the popular segment. The brandy portfolio has been moved into the P&A segment, with prior periods restated. Management reiterated a double-digit P&A growth aspiration for FY27, relying on the Maharashtra lap, the MML brand launches and innovation in H2, and kept the DJ-related deal on track for a mid-December longstop date.

financial_highlights.metric: West Asia crisis cost impact, Q2

segments.name: P&A (Prestige & Above, now incl. brandy)
segments.commentary: Price-mix of 7.4% led by luxury and premium scotches, including relaunched GNB; the segment now includes brandy after restatement. Management expects H2 to be stronger than H1.

segments.name: Popular segment
segments.commentary: Under 10% of revenue and about 6% in Q2. Hit by continued Maharashtra policy impact and full impact of Karnataka policy changes. Management has no plans to exit or intervene, since it is largely the McDowell's trademark.

guidance_outlook: Management retains a double-digit P&A growth aspiration for FY27, which implies about 12% growth in H2 per management's arithmetic.
Maharashtra lap adds about 2-3 points to growth from the current quarter; MML brands lap from the next quarter, adding about 2-3 points.
Gross margin expected to hold sequentially in Q3, with FTA benefit offsetting rising neutral alcohol spirit (ENA) costs.
Core portfolio marketing spend guided at about 11% of net sales; new platforms such as RTD and small-pack ice sit on top of this.
BCCI approval awaited; closing expected by the extended longstop date in mid-December.
Festive season is delayed this year; November-December will capture the demand for the current fiscal year.
capex_capacity: Management did not discuss capex or capacity additions in the call.
Tamil Nadu: management said it would be ready in about 45 days if the market opens, citing past Telangana/Andhra-style agility, and has some manufacturing and presence already.
demand_pricing: Lower-end consumer (India 1) showing fatigue from inflation; premium and luxury demand (India 2 and 3) strong.
Karnataka policy shift (16 slabs to 8) improved pricing flexibility; popular segment still hurt.
Price cuts on imported (BIO) brands are reaching consumers now, with states approving excise cost cards; response to be seen over the next 3-4 months.
FSSAI plant visits diverted bandwidth and disrupted supply in Q2; management says this issue is now resolved.
McDowell's acceptance issue in large states: packaging changes are reaching the market and improvement is seen market by market in November.
Competition heating up in scotch and vodka-type categories; management cited new Smirnoff flavoured launches at 4.8% and 8% ABV.
Neutral alcohol spirit was deflationary in Q1 FY27, flat YoY in Q2, and expected to turn inflationary due to El Nino.

qa_highlights.question: Why keep the popular segment (about 6% of revenue) given margin pressure and low viability?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is largely the McDowell's trademark, which is managed as one trademark. It sees the growth pool in prestige and has no plans to intervene; the segment may decline naturally.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the DRI investigation on scotch import classification and impact on the UK FDA-related benefit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the company has classified scotch imports under the same HSN code for 15-20 years, is cooperating, and is confident in its classification. Consignments have been clearing since July 15.

qa_highlights.question: What is the timeline for the BCCI approval and the deal close?
qa_highlights.answer: The longstop date was extended by two months to mid-December. Management is hopeful of closing by that date given advanced BCCI engagement.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sequential gross margin expansion from Q1 to Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Category and premiumisation mix plus FTA benefit flowing into the P&L from July 15. Management declined to quantify the FTA benefit in basis points.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to double-digit P&A growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Maharashtra lap adds 2-3 points, MML brands add 2-3 points, and the balance comes from McDowell's and innovation. Management said it is too early to call whether McDowell's can reach 7-8% growth.

qa_highlights.question: Is the excess marketing spend the new normal, and what is the full-year ad spend guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: The 11.6% marketing rate is the new normal for FY27. Core portfolio spend is guided at about 11%, with new platforms on top.

risks_watch: DRI/customs classification probe on scotch imports; management says any adverse outcome would be material and would be disclosed.
BCCI approval and deal closing by mid-December longstop date.
ENA and crop-driven inflation from El Nino and weak monsoon could compress gross margin after the FTA benefit runs out.
State excise revenue protection could reverse or limit BIO price cut benefits.
Weak lower-end consumer demand and the popular segment policy headwinds in Maharashtra and Karnataka.
Competition in the premium and vodka segments and the pace of McDowell's recovery.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the premium portfolio and H2 recovery, but cautious on the lower-end consumer and input costs. Management was evasive on quantifying the FTA benefit and on the DRI probe details, and it kept the BCCI timeline to the extended longstop date.
key_quotes: So sequentially, I'll probably say the gross margin should hold, right, for the coming quarter.
The marketing reinvestment rate during the quarter was 11.6% of net sales, which is an expansion of 400 basis points compared to prior year of same quarter.
We are hopeful, right? Because through the engagement levels of BCCI, we know we are at a fairly advanced stage, right?
